title: Stink Bugs in Your House Every Fall? How and Why They're There
description:

They get in during September. You notice them in January. That gap is the whole reason winter spraying does nothing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE GAP SIZES, AND WHEN TO CLOSE THEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT FITS THROUGH WHAT
• Stink bug, cluster fly: 1/8 in — sealant, weatherstrip, screen repair
• House mouse: 1/4 in — copper mesh or coarse stainless wool packed tight, sealed over
• Snake: 1/4 in — same as mice; they are following the mice
• Bat: 3/8 in — check for young inside and check your local law BEFORE sealing
• Rat: 1/2 in — hardware cloth or sheet metal; they chew through foam and sealant
• Squirrel: 1 1/2 in — sheet metal or hardware cloth

THE TIMING THAT DECIDES IT
Do the sealing in LATE SUMMER, before the autumn window opens. Sealing in January
locks in what is already inside and changes nothing about next year.

WHERE TO LOOK, IN ORDER
• Every penetration through the exterior wall — hose bibs, electrical, gas, cable,
  AC lines, dryer vents
• Where the siding meets the foundation, all the way round, at ground level
• Under and behind exterior steps and the deck ledger
• Garage door bottom and side seals
• Crawl space vents and hatch — are the screens intact?
• Roofline: gable vents, soffit joins, where a roof meets a wall

THE FREE VERSION OF THE AUDIT
Walk the outside after dark with the interior lights on. Light gets out wherever
they get in.
